audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers repeatedly attribute a knockup to K'Sante's Q. 'his Q knockup' / 'Q knockups' / 'Q wall-knockups' / 'Get walled by his Q' appear in full.tldr, full.dosFull[2].t, full.dontsFull[0].t, content.early, content.whys[0], content.whys[1], content.spikes[0].text, content.wants.you[0] and content.wants.foe[0]. Ntofo Strikes has no knockup and no stun.
audit.why: Ntofo Strikes damages and slows in a short line and grants a stack; at 2 stacks it fires a shockwave that PULLS enemies in. The knockback-and-stun is on Path Maker (W), and the wall-launch is on All Out (R). A Nasus told to dodge a Q knockup will stand in exactly the wrong place and eat the W stun instead. The pull arriving only on the SECOND Ntofo Strikes is also the concrete tell nobody wrote down.
audit.corrected: Ntofo Strikes (Q) slows, and pulls only on its second stack. Path Maker (W) is the knockback and stun. All Out (R) is what launches you through a wall.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json Q, W and R descriptions and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late, content.whys[5] and content.spikes[3].text all cite a 'percent-HP passive' that supposedly eats Nasus's health bar. K'Sante has no percent-health damage anywhere in his kit.
audit.why: Dauntless Instinct marks targets to take more damage from his next attack, and amplifies his damage while All Out — no max-health scaling. The K'Sante kit carries no percentHealth flag at all. What actually ignores Nasus's defences is Path Maker's true damage. This matters for itemisation: 'his passive eats HP' points you toward armour, and armour is precisely what Path Maker walks through.
audit.corrected: Path Maker deals true damage — armour does not answer it. Dauntless Instinct is an ability-into-attack damage mark, not percent health.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json P description and W trueDamage flag

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid says his ult 'drops a wall behind you so you can't walk away'; content.whys[4] and content.spikes[1].text say it 'walls off your retreat'. All Out builds no wall.
audit.why: All Out knocks the target back, launching them through any wall in their path, then K'Sante dashes after them. The isolation comes from being thrown somewhere, not from terrain being created. Standing away from walls is the actual counterplay, and you cannot derive that from 'he drops a wall'.
audit.corrected: All Out knocks you back and slams you through the nearest wall — fight him in open ground, not with terrain at your back.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Path Maker stops stunning once K'Sante is All Out.
audit.why: Riot's own text: 'When All Out, deals increased damage and no longer knocks back or stuns.' Once he ults, his remaining hard CC is Ntofo Strikes' second-stack pull and the initial R knockback. For a Nasus whose whole plan is to survive to a stacked Q, knowing the CC actually thins out inside his ult changes whether the R duel is survivable.
audit.corrected: Inside All Out, Path Maker loses its knockback and stun.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds guidance anywhere despite All Out granting him healing.
audit.why: All Out gives increased damage, healing and transformed abilities at the cost of reduced defences. The reduced-defence half is already half-noted in the file; the healing half is missing entirely, and it is the half that decides the extended fight Nasus is trying to force.
audit.corrected: All Out heals him — bring Grievous Wounds before you commit to the long duel.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carries one generic line with no numbers.
audit.why: All Out is 120/100/80s, Path Maker 14/13/12/11/10s, Footwork 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s and Ntofo Strikes only 3.5s flat. The 3.5s Q is why you never get a clean window by waiting for it — you wait for Path Maker instead.
audit.corrected: All Out 120/100/80. Path Maker 14/13/12/11/10 is the cooldown worth tracking; Ntofo Strikes at 3.5s never really goes down.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early and content.wants.foe[2] describe Path Maker as a 'block' that eats your autos.
audit.why: It is a charge-up with damage reduction, then a dash. Framing it as a block invites the player to wait it out at melee range; the accurate framing is that dumping an empowered Siphoning Strike into the charge wastes your one big hit into his tankiest moment.
audit.corrected: Path Maker takes reduced damage while it charges — do not spend a stacked Q into it.

audit.why: 49.19% over 559 games, and the level chart (K'Sante levels 1-first item, Nasus at 2+ items) is a fair read of a near-even scaling matchup.

edits.before: Dodge his Q knockups — farm stacks and Wither his R duel. Nasus wins by trading around K'Sante's All Out and cashing the pattern: out-stack and Wither his R duel.
edits.after: Dodge Path Maker's stun — farm stacks and Wither his R duel. Nasus wins by trading around K'Sante's All Out and cashing the pattern: out-stack and Wither his R duel.

edits.before: - K'Sante All Out: matchup-defining — His duelist mode. Wither him in it. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - All Out: 120/100/80s. Inside it Path Maker loses its stun, so his only hard CC is Ntofo Strikes' pull.

edits.before: K'Sante owns the first three levels and you just have to accept it — his Q knockup into the W-charge dash chunks you before you have Wither, and there's nothing you can punish. Don't try to trade Q-for-Q early; he blocks your big autos with W and the knockup interrupts everything. Sit behind Spirit Fire, let the lingering DoT clear the wave, and farm Siphoning Strike stacks at max range. Take the poke and stay healthy on your Soul Eater lifesteal.
edits.after: K'Sante owns the first three levels and you just have to accept it — Ntofo Strikes (Q) pulls you in on its second stack and Path Maker (W) stuns, and you have nothing to answer with. Don't trade Q-for-Q early; Path Maker takes reduced damage while it charges, so your big autos land into his tankiest second. Sit behind Spirit Fire, let the lingering DoT clear the wave, and farm Siphoning Strike stacks at max range. Take the poke and stay healthy on Soul Eater lifesteal.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 stay his — he's stronger in every extended trade and at 6 his R isolates you, strips his own armor and MR for raw damage, and drops a wall behind you so you can't walk away. Do not get caught alone for that ult. Once you have Wither at 3 you can at least peel a gank or punish a wildly overextended dash, but you don't own the lane. Use Wither's attack-speed slow on him in any forced fight and grind farm; your job here is to survive his power window, not contest it.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 stay his — he's stronger in every extended trade and at 6 All Out knocks you back through the nearest wall, strips his own armour and MR for raw damage, and heals him while he chases. Do not get caught alone for that ult. Once you have Wither at 3 you can at least peel a gank or punish a wildly overextended Footwork dash, but you don't own the lane. Use Wither's attack-speed slow in any forced fight and grind farm; your job is to survive his power window, not contest it.

edits.before: This is where it flips back to you. Once your Siphoning Strike stacks pile up and Fury of the Sands is online, you out-duel most of the roster in a sustained fight, and Wither shuts down his kite. Bait his W-block with a normal auto, then land the empowered Q when his cooldowns are spent. The one caveat: K'Sante is a real scaler too — his percent-HP passive eats your big HP bar and his fighter-form item spike can reclaim trades, so don't fight him even at his items, force it on yours and end before he gets there.
edits.after: This is where it flips back to you. Once your Siphoning Strike stacks pile up and Fury of the Sands is online, you out-duel most of the roster in a sustained fight, and Wither shuts down his kite. Bait Path Maker with a normal auto, then land the empowered Q while it is on cooldown. Two caveats: All Out heals him, so Grievous Wounds decides the long fight, and Path Maker deals true damage that ignores every point of armour you buy — but All Out strips his own resists, so that is when your stacked Q hits hardest.

edits.after: Both of you are weak level-1 melee with no ult, so it's a coin-flip last-hit stage — soak Q stacks and stay outside Ntofo Strikes' 450 range.

notes: The packet's single suspectName here ('Spirit Fire's' in wants.you[0]) is a FALSE POSITIVE — correct name plus a possessive. The genuine defects were much larger: K'Sante's Q is credited with a knockup nine times across both layers when the knockback/stun is Path Maker (W) and the wall-launch is All Out (R), and a non-existent 'percent-HP passive' is cited three times. The percent-HP error is the dangerous one — it steers the player toward armour, which is exactly what Path Maker's true damage ignores. All nine Q-knockup instances are covered by the edits below. The packet defect 'never names any of K'Sante's abilities' is also resolved — the content layer now names Ntofo Strikes, Path Maker, Footwork and All Out.
